lead: A module doc's `# What is not here yet` is as likely to be stale as to be a real gap.
body: The prose was written before the goal that built the member, and nothing re-reads a paragraph when code lands under it, so a section listing unregistered members often describes a surface that is registered and tested today. Grep the registry, the lexer or the symbol the paragraph names before writing one up as a gap with an owner: what has landed becomes prose, and only what the code still refuses becomes a `# Known gaps` item.
